title: Personal Checking: Standing Requirements for a Conversion to Private Client Checking
content:
## Requirements that stay in force

An owner's request to move a Personal Checking account into Private Client Checking must satisfy every ordinary requirement of a customer-requested conversion, unchanged:

- the account is in active status;
- the owner's age reaches Private Client Checking's youngest opening age;
- the owner holds fewer Private Client Checking accounts than that tier's per-customer ceiling, and the conversion keeps the owner within the product-wide ceiling on checking accounts;
- no other customer-requested conversion has already been made on this account during the current statement cycle.

If any one of these fails, no conversion is written, however large the owner's balances may be.

## How the once-per-cycle limit is evidenced

The checking records hold the account's present tier but no dated history of earlier conversions. The limit is therefore judged on two sources together: conversions recorded during the current contact, and any conversion the owner says was made earlier in the same cycle. If neither shows one, the limit is satisfied.

## Checklist view

| Requirement | Where it is read | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Account active | account record | no conversion |
| Age at or above the youngest opening age | date of birth on the customer profile | no conversion |
| Private Client account count under the tier ceiling, and product-wide count respected | the customer's checking accounts and their statuses | no conversion |
| No earlier customer-requested conversion this cycle | conversions recorded in this contact, plus the owner's own report | no conversion |

## Hypothetical case

Earlier in this contact the owner had the account moved from Everyday Checking to Interest Checking. A second request, now to Private Client Checking, fails the once-per-cycle limit and is not recorded, whatever the balances show.
